sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: About Binumarien, not Kambaira. p. 517: 'The closely related language of Kambaira is to the southeast.' Binumarien is described with two phonemic tone levels (p. 519); nothing whatsoever is said about Kambaira stress or tone.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [page last modified 2024-06-25]. Kambaira. New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute), https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/trans-new-guinea/eastern-highlands-kratke-range/eastern-highlands/kainantu/west-kainantu/north-kainantu/kambaira
sources.note: Nothing. Section 'Phonology' infers 8 consonants (m n p t k ʔ β ɾ) and 5-6 vowels plus two diphthongs from 'Vincent (n.d.) 97 terms for Kambaira'; discusses sound changes shared with North Tairora and Binumarien loans; no word for stress, accent, tone or pitch anywhere on the page. States 'Nothing is known about Kambaira verbal morphology.' Population 135 (1959-60) after Wurm & Laycock 1961: 139.

No grammar, sketch or phonology exists in Glottolog's bibliography.
